rows.question: Why did activation drop in February?

report.summary: February activation was lower: 60.0% versus 72.5% in the baseline (s1, s2). The reported splits attribute more of the change to rates within groups than to mix, but the available evidence does not establish why those rates changed; release timing alone is not proof of cause (s1, s2, s4).

observed_changes.text: Activation was 60.0% in February versus 72.5% in the baseline (s1, s2).

The segment split reports +1.1 points from segment mix and +11.4 points from within-segment rates; the channel split reports +2.3 points from channel mix and +10.2 points from within-channel rates (s1, s2).
Mid-market went from 41% to 27% of segment mix, and invite went from 75% to 56% of channel mix (s1, s2).

possible_explanations.text: A product behaviour change may have affected activation within some groups; the splits attribute more change to within-group rates than to mix (s1, s2).
possible_explanations.confidence_reason: Within-group rate changes are reported, but no evidence links them to a product change. The nearby release is timing only, and some group samples are small (s1, s2, s4).
possible_explanations.conflicting: The evidence does not show a consistent decline across all groups, and there were no matching onboarding feedback records (s1, s2, s5).

possible_explanations.text: A change in who entered each segment or channel may have contributed to the overall result (s1, s2).
possible_explanations.confidence_reason: Mix did change, but the reported mix contributions are smaller than the within-group rate contributions (s1, s2).
possible_explanations.conflicting: The splits attribute more change to within-group rates than to mix, so mix alone is not a strong explanation (s1, s2).

possible_explanations.text: A tracking or measurement issue could have affected the rates, but the checks do not establish one (s3).
possible_explanations.confidence_reason: No low-volume days were flagged, but that check does not rule out other tracking or measurement gaps (s3).
possible_explanations.conflicting: No low-volume days were flagged in February (s3).

conflicting_evidence.text: The reported segment and channel splits attribute more of the change to within-group rates than to mix, weakening a mix-only explanation (s1, s2).
The release record says the nearby release timing is not evidence of cause, and the feedback search found no matching records (s4, s5).

ruled_out.text: Portfolio filters was released on 2025-03-05, after the February window, so it cannot explain the February change (s4).

data_quality.text: Fewer than 30 records were reported for Individual, Mid-market, SMB, partner, and sales in a period; treat those rates as noisy (s1, s2).
No low-volume days were flagged, but the check does not assess every possible tracking issue (s3).
The search found 0 feedback records mentioning onboarding, activation, or signup in Onboarding; absence of matches does not establish absence of friction (s5).

suggested_experiments: Compare activation by segment and channel using larger samples and the same definitions across periods to test whether within-group changes persist (s1, s2).
Audit activation-event instrumentation and event completeness for February against the baseline (s3).
Review the Workspace verification checklist change with a controlled exposure or rollback comparison before attributing any effect to it (s4).
limitations: The baseline and February windows differ, and the supplied results do not establish a causal comparison (s1, s2).
Several subgroup samples are small, reducing confidence in their rates (s1, s2).
The release record and feedback search provide limited causal evidence (s4, s5).
